input.quote: Subject to the licenses and rights of reference granted under Sections 5.1 and 5.2 and, in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder, each Party shall have the right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party.
input.rationale: The IP allocation meets our preferred position and nothing assigns our IP or data to Harpoon. Section 7.1.1 (p0427–p0428) confirms each Party owns and retains all right, title and interest in the Information, inventions, Patents and other IP it makes or already controls, so AbbVie keeps both its background IP and the IP it generates; Harpoon keeps its platform, which the playbook expressly accepts. Section 3.8.2(c) (p0327) gives AbbVie sole ownership of all Regulatory Documentation, Regulatory Approvals and Product Labeling specific to the Licensed Compounds/Products, with a Harpoon further-assurances/assignment covenant — i.e. we own the key data and dossier deliverable. Section 5.2 (p0358) grants Harpoon only a non-exclusive, royalty-free, non-sublicensable licence to AbbVie IP limited to performing its Initial Development Plan obligations, not an assignment. Section 7.1.2 does create joint ownership of jointly-made Joint Know-How/Joint Patents, but each Party may Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without consent from or accounting to the other (and Harpoon remains bound by its exclusivity covenant), so this is joint ownership with an unrestricted right to exploit and therefore outside walk-away territory. Two points noted but not flagged: the closing proviso of Section 7.1.2 and parts of Section 12.7.1 are redacted, and the Section 12.7.1 reversion is a royalty-bearing licence (not an assignment) of AbbVie Reversion IP triggered only on termination other than by AbbVie for cause/under Section 12.4 — a customary reversion licence that does not transfer ownership of our IP.
